One of the latest cases comes out of the University of Kentucky, where a research administrator
was granted an exemption from using AI at work, citing his deeply held humanist beliefs.
Whitney Barth, a professor at Emory Law School, says granting those exemptions could become

An employer has to accommodate religion, except if it leads to substantial increased cost in

Elon Musk's company Neuralink is reporting early results for a trial of its brain implant,
as NPR's Ping Wong reports it's focused on helping those with speech difficulties.
ALS, also known as Lou Gehrig's disease, is a neurological disorder.
Patients lose their ability to speak and move.
Over the past year, in the so-called voice trial, three patients with ALS received Neuralink
implants, which pick up brain signals that get processed into sound, words and sentences.
Dr. Nader Peradian, at UT Southwestern, is principal investigator.
He hopes to apply it more broadly, which means recruiting more patients with other diagnoses
so we can learn more about how it's the same or how it might be different and how we might
have to customize it for those different populations, such as those who have had spinal cord injuries
or stroke.
Peradian says they're still working on the implant's ability to discern thoughts a patient
wants to share from those they do not.
The results, presented at an ALS conference, have not yet been peer-reviewed.
Ping Wong, NPR News.
